newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding reserves via system repurchases.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding reserves via system repurchases.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is likely to add temporary reserves to the open market on Monday through multi-day system repurchase agreements, analysts said.

Dean Witter Reynolds money market research estimates the Fed's add need at $2.5 billion a day for the rest of the bank reserve maintenance period, ending on Wednesday. As a result, they expect the Fed to add temporary reserves to the banking system through multi-day system repurchases.
Patricia Thrapp, vice president at Aubrey G. Lanston & Co, expects the Fed to add temporary reserves through three-day system repurchases.

"I have an add need of just over $4.0 billion per day for the rest of the week," said Thrapp. "I'm looking for a three-day system repurchase operation, not fixed. They might have to replace some reserves again on Wednesday."
Michael Englund, chief economist at MMS International, looks for some moderate pressures on bank reserves going into the period-end on Wednesday.

But Englund, noting that Federal funds are trading at 5-1/4 percent, the Fed's target for the rate, said he expects the Fed to add temporary reserves via system repurchases on Tuesday and Wednesday -- and to refrain from action on Monday.
